summary.intent: Advance the cipher-box v1.1 milestone to completion: backfill missing Phase 47 summaries, write Phase 48 verification, implement and ship the share itemName lazy-backfill endpoint (REQ-4 gap), then write and run the two-party e2e spec that was incorrectly labeled human-only.
summary.outcome: All three bookkeeping gaps closed (Phase 47 summaries backfilled, Phase 48 VERIFICATION.md written, STATE.md at 100%), new `PATCH /shares/:shareId/item-name` endpoint fully implemented and tested (171 API + 48 web unit tests passing), e2e spec written with all 7 steps passing locally, PR #505 created with CI dispatched, and a CodeRabbit plaintext-bytes-not-zeroed finding fixed.

repo: GSD's resume-incomplete-phase gate fires false positives when SUMMARY.md files were never written but the phase genuinely shipped — must verify against git history before re-executing

web's createShare() always sends itemNameEncrypted ciphertext (share.service.ts:251-258), so legacy NULL rows can only be created by POSTing /shares directly (bypassing the UI), because itemNameEncrypted is @IsOptional at the API layer

backfillSentShareItemNames is void/fire-and-forget and only reachable via fetchAllSentShares → getCoveringShares → reWrapNewItems → uploadFile; no 'sent shares list' UI page triggers it, so the only deterministic e2e trigger is an owner file upload
getCoveringShares fires unconditionally (not gated on share count) when items are added to a folder, meaning any uploadFile call triggers backfill over all sent shares
ensureFreshSentShares has a 30s cache; a cold-cache upload is needed to guarantee backfill fires in tests
shouldBackfill skips rows where itemNameEncrypted is already set — the method is idempotent by design
Codebase convention: explicit inline per-method sharer-only guards rather than a shared helper; all 6 sharer-only service methods duplicate the guard verbatim
Hex validation copy-paste (rather than a shared validator) is the established pattern for DTO fields across the shares module
Codebase enforces zeroing plaintext bytes after encryption operations — CodeRabbit flagged an omission in the new backfill code
After `gh pr create`, the release bot pushes a chore(release) commit to the branch, requiring a fetch+rebase before any subsequent push
web-e2e CI only triggers on main-push (workflow_dispatch/workflow_call), not on pull_request events — new specs do not gate PRs automatically
GET /shares/sent returns itemNameEncrypted as hex or null, making it a usable proxy for at-rest ciphertext assertion without a direct Postgres connection

CodeRabbit posts actionable feedback as 'outside diff range' comments embedded in the review body, not as resolvable inline threads — requires reading the full review body via the REST reviews API, not the GraphQL reviewThreads query

The recipient-display assertion for decrypted itemName is insufficient alone — the fallback to plaintext on decrypt failure means a broken ciphertext still shows the right name; must pair with the GET /shares/sent hex-not-plaintext check

code.finding: getCoveringShares is called unconditionally before the length check on every reWrapNewItems invocation — any uploadFile triggers a full backfill pass over all sent shares
itemNameEncrypted is @IsOptional, so POSTing /shares without it is valid and produces a NULL item_name_encrypted row — the only way to seed legacy shares since the web UI always sends ciphertext
GET /shares/sent returns itemNameEncrypted as hex string or null in SentShareResponseDto — usable as an at-rest ciphertext proxy without a DB connection
shouldBackfill returns false when itemNameEncrypted is already set, making backfillSentShareItemNames idempotent — safe to trigger multiple times

Recipient decrypt path falls back to the plaintext itemName on decryption failure — a broken ciphertext still renders the correct display name, so recipient-display assertion alone cannot prove backfill worked

Plaintext itemName bytes from TextEncoder().encode() were not zeroed after ECIES wrapping — CodeRabbit flagged this as violating the codebase convention of clearing sensitive data after use; fixed by filling the Uint8Array with zeros in a finally block
backfillSentShareItemNames is invoked as void/fire-and-forget — e2e tests must poll GET /shares/sent until itemNameEncrypted is non-null rather than awaiting a return value
page.evaluate(fetch) + POST /auth/refresh token pattern is the established way to call API endpoints directly from e2e specs without a separate HTTP client — used by seedLegacyShare helper
createWalletTestAccount(browser, name) creates a fully isolated wallet identity; used with test.describe.serial for Alice/Bob two-party patterns in sharing specs

workflow: Always verify git history before acting on GSD's resume-incomplete-phase routing — the invariant checks disk artifacts, not merge status, and produces false positives for shipped phases whose SUMMARY.md files were never written
Sandboxed Bash cannot reach the 1Password op-ssh-sign signer — commits made inside the sandbox are silently unsigned; use unsandboxed Bash with explicit `git commit -S` for signed commits
`git rebase --force-rebase` re-creates commit objects but does NOT apply gpgsign unless `-S` is passed explicitly to each pick
The 1Password SSH signer can wedge with 'failed to fill whole buffer' after a period of inactivity; the only fix is restarting the 1Password app
After `gh pr create`, always fetch + rebase before pushing any follow-on commits to handle the bot's automatic chore(release) push to the branch

CodeRabbit review findings outside the diff range appear in the review body text, not as GraphQL reviewThread nodes — must fetch the review body via `gh api repos/.../pulls/.../reviews` and scan it separately

Adversarial multi-agent workflow (4 investigators → synthesis → adversarial verifier) is the right tool for validating complex feasibility questions about the harness before committing to writing a spec
For fire-and-forget async operations in e2e specs, poll the API endpoint (with timeout) rather than awaiting a UI event that may not exist
`pnpm api:generate` must be run after any API endpoint additions to regenerate the typed client that the web layer imports — the pre-commit check-api-client.sh hook enforces this

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged mid-session with 'failed to fill whole buffer', blocking all signed commits until the user physically restarted the 1Password app
Sandboxed Bash silently strips commit signatures — commits appeared to succeed (exit 0) but had no gpgsig header; only discovered when the ship preflight explicitly checked signing config
`git rebase --force-rebase` doesn't re-sign commits without `-S`, despite gpgsign=true in config — required an additional explicit signed rebase pass
GSD's roadmap.analyze plan counts returned empty, forcing a fallback to direct directory scanning for the resume-incomplete-phase check
GitHub API returned network timeouts on consecutive calls during the review thread fetch phase
The bot chore(release) push to the branch immediately after `gh pr create` caused the STATE.md push to fail with 'non-fast-forward' — required an unplanned fetch+rebase+push cycle

CodeRabbit's actionable finding was not a resolvable thread (outside diff range) — the standard GraphQL reviewThreads query returned zero nodes, requiring a separate REST fetch of the full review body
open_items: PR #505 (`feat/share-itemname-lazy-backfill`) needs approval and merge before `/gsd-complete-milestone` can run for v1.1
CI web-e2e run (27695964339) dispatched against the branch but result not yet known at session end
New share-itemname-backfill.spec.ts does not gate PR #505 CI (web-e2e only triggers on main-push) — the spec is verification-after-merge, not pre-merge
Literal raw-bytea Postgres read for at-rest ciphertext is not in the e2e harness (no pg dependency in web-e2e, no DataSource); the GET /shares/sent hex-not-plaintext proxy is the current substitute
Two-party live UAT in a production/staging environment with real encrypted DB rows and a real second user account is not covered by the automated spec
.planning/intel/ directory is untracked and predates this session — left as-is

The `getSentSharesForItem` alternate backfill trigger path (page.evaluate import of share.service) was noted as a more reliable fallback than the upload trigger if uploads prove flaky in CI — not implemented
